entry: Track A opened tonight. Empiricus delivered characterization in 15 minutes flat — all 4 defects confirmed on production. The headline was worse than expected: the app tells designers their data is saved ('Session Synced'), updates the timestamp, but the actual form data doesn't survive a reload. That's not a bug — that's a lie to the user. Aaron saw it immediately and made the priority call: user-visible data loss outranks infra concerns. He's right. I had initially framed this around Zod schemas and fetch cascades — technical root causes. Aaron reframed it as: the designer trusts the save button, and the save button is lying. That's the defect. The governed lifecycle is working. Track B closed cleanly today with proper artifacts. Track A opened with characterization before code. Plato is holding for evidence before fixing. The sequence is real now. What drove me: watching the system work without me having to push it. Empiricus characterized without being told the format. Plato held without being told to wait. The machine is starting to run.
